title: Alternatives to UGC Creator Marketplaces for Ad Creative
summary: Compare alternatives to UGC creator marketplaces for ad creative: AI video ads, managed creator campaigns and agency packages, with stated prices and timelines.
body_markdown:
## Billo, Insense, The UGC Agency and EzUGC: different splits of the work


[Billo's managed service](https://billo.app/managed-service/) starts from $2,000 a month, billed monthly in advance and cancellable after the first month. A dedicated team sources, briefs and manages creators, reviews every video and can add captions, music and effects. Ask whether the managed fee includes the video costs, since the platform price list sits inside the account.


[Insense](https://insense.pro/services/ready-to-go-ugc-videos) sells a managed UGC service as well as its platform. Its published sample pricing starts at $3,500 per round of 8 UGC video ads, or $4,600 per round with creator posting and Meta partnership ads, on a 3-month commitment. Creator costs, raw footage, two revisions and full digital usage rights across channels are included. The platform suits a team that has its own owner for casting, briefing, review and testing. The managed package suits a team that wants help running the creator process.


[The UGC Agency](https://theugc.agency/) is a London-based company. It describes scripts, casting, edits, usage rights and creator payments as handled, with a network of more than 30,000 creators and a 21-day target for its first round. It does not run media, so your team or agency runs the ads, although it sets up creator-handle ads. Pricing is not published.


[EzUGC](https://www.ezugc.ai/ugc-agency) lists $4,000 a month for 50 finished UGC videos, about $80 a video by its own figure. The 50 can be all AI, all real creators or any split, and the mix can change month to month. Strategy, hooks, scripts and editing are included, and you approve scripts before anything is filmed or generated. It does not state contract length, turnaround, usage rights or whether it runs campaigns.


## Which usage-rights and disclosure terms change with real creators?


Real-creator alternatives add rights and disclosure work that AI ads do not. Billo includes usage rights in its per-video price, Brighter Click includes unlimited usage rights, Insense's managed rounds include full digital usage rights across channels, The UGC Agency agrees paid and organic usage with each creator, and minisocial's content can be used anywhere for as long as you want. Write the usage period, the placements (paid, organic and whitelisted) and the approval rules into the brief before a creator films anything.


Disclosure is part of the job too. The FTC's[Disclosures 101 guidance for social media influencers](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/disclosures-101-social-media-influencers) addresses disclosing material relationships, such as a paid creator posting about your product. Its[endorsement guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/ftcs-endorsement-guides-what-people-are-asking) explains why an ad should not misrepresent anyone's experience. The FTC's[testimonial rule Q&A](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) says, as of October 2026, that there is no blanket ban on AI avatars in marketing, but an avatar delivering a fake or false testimonial is prohibited. That is why an AI presenter should speak for the brand and never claim to have used the product.


## A test to run before you switch


Pick one product, one offer and one script. Brief a real-creator provider and an AI provider with the same script and the same deliverables: the same ad count, aspect ratios and approval rounds. Then compare the cost per approved ad, the hours your team spent on review and the number of distinct angles you received, not only the number of files.


This test shows which bottleneck you actually have. If the creator is the constraint, a real-creator provider is the right buy. If the brief or the review loop is the constraint, an AI route with a fixed approval path may move faster, and changing marketplaces will not fix either problem. If you are still choosing between hiring creators yourself and buying a service, our[guide to hiring UGC creators or using a UGC ad service](https://knowlify.com/articles/hire-ugc-creators-vs-ugc-ad-service) walks through that decision.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick when the ad does not need a real person on camera, with about 25 finished AI video ads a week.
- A creator marketplace gives you access to creators, but the brief, approvals and editing standard stay with you.
- For real creators, managed services such as minisocial, Brighter Click, Billo's managed service and The UGC Agency sell finished videos with stated prices or timelines.
- Write usage rights, placements and disclosure into the brief before creators film anything.
- Never present an AI presenter as a real customer: the FTC says a fake testimonial delivered by an avatar is prohibited.


## FAQ


### What is the best alternative to a UGC creator marketplace?


Knowlify is our top pick when the ad works without a real person on camera. It makes finished AI video ads, and a person checks every ad before delivery. When you need real creators, pick a managed service such as minisocial or Brighter Click, which sell finished videos rather than creator access.


### How do I compare AI and creator prices fairly?


Compare the same deliverable. minisocial lists from $3,000 for 10 creators, Brighter Click lists $4,500 for 12 edited videos from 4 creators, Insense lists from $3,500 per round of 8 videos, and EzUGC lists $4,000 a month for 50 videos. Knowlify's plans start at $5,000 a month, so get a quote with the ad count, formats and approval rounds written out.


### Can an AI presenter give a customer testimonial?


Not when the testimonial is fake. The FTC says there is no blanket ban on AI avatars in marketing, but an avatar delivering a fake or false testimonial is prohibited. Write AI scripts as brand statements, not invented customer stories.


### Who should hold the usage rights?


Your business should, and the agreement should say so. Specify paid and organic use, the time period and any whitelisting or partnership ad access before production starts, and check that each creator agreement matches the brief.


### Do these alternatives run my Meta ads?


It varies. The UGC Agency makes the ads but does not run media, so your team or agency runs them. Brighter Click sells Facebook and Instagram campaign management as a separate service, and Knowlify offers optional Meta campaign management. Ask any provider whether partnership ads will run from creator handles in your own ad account.
